reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis is scientifically sound: short-time annealing to precipitate coherent interphase films at colony boundaries is a plausible mechanism to strengthen interfaces and delay microcrack initiation, though the specific claim of simultaneous strength and ductility improvement in a notoriously brittle system is ambitious and depends on a narrow, unproven processing window.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and includes a decisive falsification criterion (no simultaneous improvement in strength and ductility), but the annealing parameters (700 °C, 30–50 s, 15 K/s) are given without justification and may be impractical to control precisely in bulk samples, weakening the feasibility.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis addresses a critical bottleneck in eutectic HEAs and proposes a novel, targeted interfacial engineering approach that, if validated, would be highly valuable to researchers in the field.
